case_studies.title: Balancing Usefulness and Naturalness: An LLM-based Curation Pipeline for Code Review Comments
case_studies.abstract: Code review is a cornerstone of software development, where reviewers provide feedback through written comments to ensure code quality, maintainability, and correctness. The effectiveness of this process hinges on the quality of review comments. As large language models (LLMs) gain traction in automating code review tasks, the utility of these systems is directly limited by the quality of the datasets on which they are trained. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of noisy and poorly structured code review datasets by building an LLM-based curation pipeline to improve comment quality. The pipeline helps large language models generate accurate and helpful code review comments. The result is more effective code review, which can lead to better software quality and maintainability.

case_studies.title: Failure as a Process: An Anatomy of CLI Coding Agent Trajectories
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents are increasingly deployed to autonomously perform software engineering tasks in terminal-based environments, making their reliability a growing concern. Existing empirical studies investigate why coding agents fail, yet they largely treat failure as a final outcome rather than a temporal process, providing limited insight into how failures emerge, evolve, and become unrecoverable. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding how coding agent failures occur in cloud infrastructure by analyzing the process of failure, the authors built a framework to study failure trajectories, and the result provides insight into how failures emerge and evolve. It helps identify reliability concerns in large language model coding agents used in terminal-based environments. This research is relevant to IT engineers managing cloud infrastructure that use coding agents.

case_studies.title: ProofCouncil: An LLM Agent for Solving Open Mathematical Problems
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in solving open problems in mathematics. However, their performance can be further improved through agentic workflows tailored to real-world mathematical practice. To this end, we introduce ProofCouncil, a mathematical agent that is designed to tackle open problems using an author-critic architecture. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of using large language models to tackle open mathematical problems by building an agent called ProofCouncil. The result was that ProofCouncil was able to successfully solve 6 out of 10 real-world mathematical problems autonomously. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

While recent adoptions of Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated promise in penetration testing and Capture-the-Flag (CTF) environments, their application to IoT specific vulnerabilities remains unexplored. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of vulnerable Internet of Things (IoT) systems by building an autonomous framework called VEXAIoT, which uses AI agents to discover and exploit vulnerabilities, resulting in a scalable and adaptive security testing approach. This research aims to improve the security of IoT systems by providing a new method for vulnerability detection.

case_studies.summary: Research solved the problem of high costs associated with using large language models by building smaller models with automated harness adaptation, resulting in 90% cheaper agents. This breakthrough enables more sustainable large-scale deployment of language models.

case_studies.title: Practical Source Code Recovery from Binary Functions Using Anchor-Based Retrieval and LLM Reasoning
case_studies.abstract: We present a practical pipeline for recovering source code from stripped binary functions by combining reverse engineering, anchor-based source code retrieval, and large language model reasoning. Our binary-to-source-code retrieval method attempts to identify the source function from a source code database, rather than generating approximate decompiled pseudocode. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of recovering source code from binary functions, creating a pipeline that combines reverse engineering and large language model reasoning to identify the original source function. The researchers built a binary-to-source-code retrieval method that extracts anchors and uses an inverted-index search database to find matching source code. The result is a more accurate way to recover source code from stripped binary functions.

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of context loss in multi-turn code generation systems by introducing a shared selective persistent memory architecture, which identifies and retains relevant context from previous sessions, resulting in improved generation quality. The researchers built a system that can selectively retain and share context across sessions. This is not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work.

The researchers built a framework to analyze the effects of corrupted rewards on skill retirement. The result shows that a biased judge can silently switch off the curator, leading to a drifting library below the no-skill baseline.
